headline: Open-source MCP server gives AI live NSE + BSE stock data for 8,200+ Indian stocks
summary: Stop AI models from hallucinating stock data. This open-source MCP server provides real-time NSE + BSE market insights, fundamentals, and technicals for over 8,200 Indian stocks, supporting major LLMs like ChatGPT and Claude.
details: AI models typically lack live data, often providing outdated or incorrect stock information for markets like NSE and BSE. This new open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server addresses this by providing real-time access to over 8,200 Indian stocks, including fundamentals, technicals, and institutional flows.

The MCP standard enables AI assistants to make structured requests for external data, ensuring accuracy. This server allows leading LLMs such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok to integrate seamlessly and access current market data rather than relying on their training cut-off.

Designed for ease of use, the server runs as a Cloudflare Worker, offering global distribution without server management. This setup allows users to simply paste a URL into their AI client, bypassing complex installations typically required for MCP servers.

The server supports various client authentication methods, including short-lived HMAC and long-lived personal tokens. A clever 401 response with a WWW-Authenticate header triggers the client's built-in OAuth flow, streamlining the connection process.

A user-friendly feature ensures that failed calls due to LLM-hallucinated arguments are not charged against a user's quota. For stdio-only clients, a lightweight npm package handles communication with the Cloudflare Worker, keeping all tool logic centralized on the server for instant updates.

The project is free and open-source under the MIT license, with all 34 tools and setup guides available on GitHub. It is built as a research tool, not for trading, offering a comprehensive 326-filter fundamental and technical screener.

headline: Omni-VRAM: Open-source Voice AI platform built in Python with 28 modules
